title: Dawn queue triage and handoff digest — 2026-11-29
content:
Shift: 2026-11-29 06:00-14:00 PT
Owning shift: Evan Mercer (primary), Priya Kaur (shadow)
Environment: prod/us-west1 (primary), prod/eu-west1 (failover)

Summary (quick bullets):
- Zero sev-1 incidents during window.
- Two customer-facing errors (5xx spike on hosted inference route /v1/generate) — mitigated with temporary rate limit increase and routing to dedicated-capacity pool.
- Intermittent KV cache misses for long-context requests; observed elevated p95 latency on r3-model family.
- Runbook gap discovered for cross-region fallback when dedicated capacity is saturated. Added TODO to runbook.

Incident 1: 5xx spike on /v1/generate (11:10-11:35 PT)
- Symptom: sudden increase in 5xx responses from frontends servicing small-batch chat requests. Error rate peaked ~6% for 25 minutes.
- First alert: infra-5xx spike alert (threshold 1% 5m) at 11:09. Pager to SRE primary.
- Triage notes: logs showed transient backend grpc "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED" from dedicated pool; autoscaler lagging behind burst.
- Immediate mitigations applied:
  * Turned on emergency burst routing to warm pool (11:12) — reduced queue depth.
  * Gradual traffic drain to backup dedicated pool in another AZ (11:15-11:20) — confirmed decreased 5xx.
  * Raised soft rate-limit for paid-tier routes for 10 minutes (11:16) to allow in-flight requests to complete while autoscaler recovered.
- Observed outcome: 5xx fell back to baseline by 11:35.
- Post-shift action items: INFR-2389 created for autoscaler tuning and improved warm-pool behaviour; owner: Priya Kaur; ETA: two sprints.

Incident 2: KV cache miss surge affecting r3 models (12:40-13:05 PT)
- Symptom: increased model latency for requests >4k tokens; KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% vs normal.
- Evidence: metrics show sudden evictions on cache node grp-6 correlated with longer sequences; GC logs indicate memory pressure spikes on a subset of nodes.
- Workaround during shift:
  * Enabled selective evictions on low-priority session prefixes (12:48) to preserve hot prefixes.
  * Short-term routing of long-sequence jobs to non-quantized instance family temporarily (12:55) — costlier but lower latency.
- Next steps: schedule a scheduled maintenance window to respin grp-6 nodes with updated kernel flags to reduce page cache churn; add stress test to CI for long-sequence traffic patterns. Task assigned to Liam O'Neill (INFR-2401).

Runbook and playbook notes (edits recommended):
- Cross-region fallback runbook: currently assumes identical dedicated capacity in failover region. Reality: capacity profiles differ. Add explicit capacity-compatibility checks and mapping table.
- Autoscaler warm-pool doc: add a section for manual burst routing and an emergency checklist for raising soft rate-limits.
- KV cache runbook: document selective-eviction knob and safe defaults for long-context workloads.

Action items and owners:
- INFR-2389 (Autoscaler warm-pool tuning + warm-start tests) — owner: Priya Kaur — ETA: 2026-12-12.
- INFR-2401 (grp-6 kernel flags + long-seq stress test) — owner: Liam O'Neill — ETA: 2026-12-08.
- Runbook update PR (autoscale & cross-region mapping) — owner: Evan Mercer — draft by 2026-12-03. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/57
- Customer comms follow-up for affected tenants (small set) — owner: Sofia Alvarez — deliver by 2026-12-02.

Monitoring adjustments made during shift:
- Lowered 5xx alert threshold temporarily from 1% to 0.5% for high-sensitivity routes to capture early regressions (reverted to baseline during wrap).
- Added ad-hoc dashboard panel for kv-cache-evictions-per-node (temp panel id: OPS-KV-12) to track grp-6 while under investigation.

Escalations and stakeholders notified:
- Product: pinged (SLA team) for any customer-impacting decisions — briefed at 11:40.
- Solutions Eng: notified for customers using dedicated pools with long-context workloads (12:10) — coordinated mitigation.
- Security: not involved.

Risks to look for in next shift:
- Autoscaler may still underreact to sudden step traffic increases on r3-family models; watch warm-pool fill rate and queue depth metrics.
- KV cache node memory pressure could reappear under heavy long-seq synthetic tests; consider rolling kernel upgrades.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Is the warm-pool sizing algorithm overly conservative for r3 workloads? Need test with synthetic bursts.
- How many customer sessions are pinned to grp-6 nodes vs spread? Need tooling to map session->node.

Handoff checklist for incoming shift (EOD cadence):
- Review INFR-2389 and INFR-2401 tickets and any status updates in Jira.
- Check queue depth and p95/p99 latency for /v1/generate and r3 model family dashboards.
- Confirm that temporary rate-limit change was reverted (if not, coordinate rollback with rate-limiter owner).
- Validate that OPS-KV-12 panel shows stable eviction counts before resuming normal traffic mix.
- If any scheduled maintenance is required during their window, confirm customer impact windows and coordinate with Product.

Notes to incoming oncall (Priya):
- If you see RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED traces again, prefer routing to backup dedicated pool before raising global rate-limits.
- For KV cache memory pressure, do not reboot nodes unless coordinated — prefer selective-eviction and session routing first.
- Ping me (Evan) on Slack if autoscaler behaves unexpectedly; I have the temporary script for forced warm-pool fill.

Appendix (quick links):
- Autoscaler metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/ops/autoscaler-r3
- KV cache dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/ops/kv-cache
- Runbooks repo: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-2389

End of digest.
